prompt: protobuf allow_alias enum all values distinct numbers behavior
answer:
If every enum constant has a distinct numeric value, `allow_alias = true` has no observable effect: the enum compiles normally, and each name maps to its own number. The option only permits multiple names to share the same numeric value; without it, duplicate numeric values produce a compiler warning or rejection depending on the implementation. 

When aliases do exist, serialization/deserialization behavior differs: the first declared name is used for the numeric value, while all aliases are accepted when parsing.
